subject: Proposal: Billing model shift & term credit structure for Acme Analytics
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reeves <t.reeves@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring a shift from monthly billing to a year commit

Hi Connor,

We're evaluating a move away from our current month-to-month consumption with Redwood to a committed annual billing model for 2026. Our usage has been growing quickly (projected 3–4x by Q4) and procurement wants clarity on: term discounts, ramped consumption schedule, and any one-time credits you can offer to offset early-year overages while we ramp.

High level ask: can you provide a concession matrix showing discount tiers for 12/24-month commits at different annual committed $ levels, plus an example ramp schedule where we start at 40% of committed spend in Q1 and reach 100% by Q4? Also need an outline of billing cadence changes and any requirements for an earlier payment (prepay vs invoiced monthly against commitment).

Can you loop in whoever owns pricing and contracts? We need this for our internal procurement review next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Procurement | Acme Analytics
elena.park@acmeanalytics.com
+1 415-555-0123

Date: 2026-04-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring a shift from monthly billing to a year commit

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Monica (rev ops) and Neha (commercial) who own the concession matrix and invoicing options.

We can put together two things quickly: 1) a pricing / concession matrix showing tiered % discounts for 12- and 24-month committed ARR with example spend bands, and 2) a recommended ramp schedule and billing cadence (prepay vs monthly-invoice-applied-to-commit). Early note: we typically allow a one-time onboarding credit to soften immediate year-1 spend if the customer commits to prepaying a minimum of Q1 (or full year) — Monica will confirm acceptable credit ranges.

I'll send a proposed matrix and a short playbook for the ramp options by tomorrow EOD. If procurement's review is next Wednesday, we should be fine.

Best,

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing inputs for Acme - draft concession matrix attached

Connor / Neha — drafting a matrix attached (rw_acme_credit_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a short memo (below) with proposed allowance/constraints.

Memo (summary):
- 12-month commit: discounts between 10–18% depending on committed ARR band.
- 24-month commit: additional 3–5% on top of 12-month level for predictable, multi-year deals.
- Onboarding / ramp credit: up to 7% of year-1 committed spend if the customer prepays Q1 or full-year (applied as a bill credit over first two invoices).
- Ramp schedule option we recommend: Q1 40% of committed throughput, Q2 65%, Q3 85%, Q4 100% (this is conservative relative to their projection). Credits for missed ramp milestones are not typical; instead we offer a true-up process at quarter end to reconcile usage vs committed.
- Non-negotiables: SLA, data residency, and audit access terms remain standard; discounts tied to commit and prepayment terms only.

Approval ask: Connor — what's the max discount you can offer without further approval? We typically cap discounts at 18% for direct AE signoff; anything beyond requires Markus / CRO sign-off. Also confirm if we should require prepay to qualify for the onboarding credit.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing inputs for Acme - draft concession matrix attached

Agree with the structure. A couple of tweaks I recommend before we share externally:
- Make 12-month mid-band the default recommended option for them (balances flexibility and economics).
- For the onboarding credit, require either Q1 prepay or signed P.O. that guarantees payment within 30 days — avoids cashflow risk.
- Add an explicit line for billing cadence: for prepay we can issue a single annual invoice with programmatic refund/credits against usage; for invoiced-commit, we invoice monthly but apply the monthly invoice against the committed balance (true-up quarterly).

Connor — for commercial sign-off: your AE authority stands at 18% discount and 7% onboarding credit with Q1 prepay. Anything greater goes to Markus.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Exploring a shift from monthly billing to a year commit — proposed options and next steps

Elena / Tom — thanks for the patience. Attached are two artifacts: 1) concession matrix (rw_acme_credit_matrix_v2.xlsx) with tiered discount levels for 12- and 24-month commits, and 2) a short pricing play (redwood_tier_pricing.pdf) that explains billing cadence and ramp examples. Key points below:

Option A — 12-month, mid-band (recommended):
- Discount: 14% on committed ARR
- Onboarding credit: 5% of year-1 committed spend if Q1 prepay or signed P.O. within 30 days
- Ramp: Q1 40%, Q2 65%, Q3 85%, Q4 100% (quarterly true-up)
- Billing: invoiced monthly, applied against committed balance; any overage billed at standard rate and reconciled quarterly

Option B — 24-month, enterprise:
- Discount: 17% on committed ARR + 3% multi-year bonus (20% total) for full-year prepay on year-1
- Onboarding credit: 7% if full-year prepay at signing
- Billing: annual prepay preferred for the additional bonus; monthly-invoice option available with same discounts but onboarding credit contingent on P.O./payment schedule

Governance / approvals: I can approve up to 18% discount and up to 7% onboarding credit if Acme either prepays Q1 or commits to a signed P.O. with payment terms acceptable to Redwood. Any request for discounts >18% or credits >7% will need Markus to sign off (I've cc'd him).

Next steps:
1) Let me know which option Acme prefers and whether procurement will prepay Q1 or sign a P.O.
2) If they approve, I'll generate a commercial summary and a DocuSign-ready SOW and route for signatures.
3) Monica will coordinate billing setup once the P.O. or payment is received.
